title: Build two-track changelog drafts and approval matrix
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Produce two parallel changelog drafts for the upcoming console release — (1) internal one-pager for ops/support/CS, and (2) customer-facing tiered changelogs (Self-serve summary + Enterprise technical notes). Deliver an approval matrix that lists required reviewers, SLAs for feedback, and final sign-off owners.

Scope & deliverables:
- Internal change brief (1 page): high-level summary, impact matrix, known regressions, rollback plan, who to page at release.
- Customer-facing short changelog (Self-serve): 2-3 bullet summary, user-facing impact, recommended actions; copy optimized for product changelog feed.
- Customer-facing technical release notes (Enterprise): detailed migration steps, compatibility notes, API contract changes, deprecation timelines, example curl/SDK snippets.
- Approval matrix: role -> required action -> SLA (e.g., Eng: technical accuracy, 48h; Legal: data/privacy review, 72h).
- Release artifacts: Google Drive drafts, GitHub PR linking to docs site, staged console changelog preview.

Key decisions so far:
- Adopt a two-track review flow: technical track (Eng -> Docs) and messaging track (PM -> Comms -> Legal). Both tracks must complete before final sign-off.
- Use the compact two-column customer format: "What changed" + "Action/Impact" to reduce support load and help CS triage.
- Enterprise notes will live behind customer login and be distributed to account teams via the Sales enablement pack.

Stakeholders & reviewers:
- Engineering leads: Priya Suresh (runtime), Mateo Alvarez (API) — technical accuracy and rollback criteria.
- Docs: Hannah Lee — copy + examples + staging to docs site.
- Comms: Carlos Mendes — messaging for changelog feed and email digest.
- Legal/Privacy: Noor Patel — required for any change touching telemetry/KMS.
- Support/CS: Maya Johnson — readiness and triage playbook.
- Design: Izzy Park — formatting and emphasis for console UI where changelog surfaces.

Gating criteria (release must meet all):
1) Technical accuracy sign-off from runtime or API lead.
2) Docs has staged markdown and example snippets validated.
3) Comms approves customer-facing tone for each audience.
4) Legal sign-off if data/telemetry/KMS touched.
5) Release engineer confirms changelog deployment hook works in staging.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Last-minute API tweaks may invalidate examples. Mitigation: freeze code changes 48h before changelog publish; include a snippet version tag.
- Risk: Conflicting feedback across reviewers causing delays. Mitigation: PM-led triage meeting 24h before due date to resolve conflicts and escalate to GTM lead.
- Risk: Enterprise customers need migration scripts. Mitigation: allocate Docs 1 sprint buffer to prepare scripts; flag high-impact accounts for SE outreach.

Acceptance criteria:
- Both drafts (internal + customer-facing) are uploaded to Drive and linked in this ticket.
- All reviewers listed in the approval matrix have recorded an explicit approval comment.
- Changelog preview is visible on staging docs site and console preview.
- Release notes page contains copy samples for SDK and REST examples where relevant.

Next steps (owners):
- Liam Chen (assignee/PM): finalize drafts and push to Drive -> due 2026-03-04.
- Priya & Mateo (Eng): validate technical accuracy and add any required migration notes -> due 2026-03-06.
- Hannah (Docs): stage markdown on docs site and run snippet smoke tests -> due 2026-03-08.
- Carlos (Comms): prepare email digest language and in-product banner copy -> due 2026-03-10.
- Noor (Legal): review if telemetry/KMS changed -> complete by 2026-03-09.

Notes: We should avoid duplicating long technical content in the short changelog; instead include a "full technical notes" link for Enterprise customers. Also recommended to include a short "If you are using Dedicated or Private deployments" callout when rollout has infra or migration steps.
